briefings.title: Academia Job Shortlist

scope.geography: United States; Cleveland/Ohio prioritized when a sufficiently strong match is available
scope.selection_rule: Include only roles that materially strengthen scientific independence, platform capability, or translational positioning.

jobs.title: Associate Staff Scientist, Intestinal Organoids
jobs.company_info: Cincinnati Children's CuSTOM ecosystem combines intestinal organoids, bioengineering, regenerative medicine, automation and translational model development.

salary.note: No reliable employer salary was surfaced in the current search; third-party estimates vary.

jobs.job_description: Develop, optimize and characterize human intestinal organoid systems in a multidisciplinary translational environment with strong links to advanced in vitro models and computational analysis.
key_must_have_requirements: PhD in biology, bioengineering, stem-cell/developmental biology, biomedical engineering or related field
Human iPSC, adult stem-cell or intestinal organoid experience
Strong quantitative and scientific communication skills
jobs.why_good_match: This is the strongest Ohio role because the user's patient-derived intestinal organoids, Crohn's models, organ-on-chip engineering and bioinformatics are all directly relevant rather than merely adjacent.
gaps_or_risks: Direct iPSC-derived intestinal organoid experience may be less extensive
Staff-scientist independence can vary widely by program
resume_tailoring: Lead with intestinal organoids and human GI models
Use organ-on-chip as the key differentiator
In the cover letter ask about first-author ownership, grant participation and advancement
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply now and contact the CuSTOM team directly; treat scientific ownership as a gating question during interviews.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow — NHP Immunology and Organ Chips
jobs.company: Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering at Harvard University
jobs.company_info: The Wyss Institute is a leading organ-chip and translational bioengineering center with direct engagement across pharma, regulators and technology translation.
jobs.term: One-year postdoctoral term with possibility of extension

salary.note: Salary follows Harvard Medical School postdoctoral guidelines based on years post-PhD.

jobs.posting_status: Active; applicants encouraged to apply by September 9, 2026
jobs.job_description: Use Organ Chip microfluidic systems to model adaptive immunity and radiation toxicity in non-human primates and humans, integrating spatial-omics and functional data and communicating results to scientific and translational stakeholders.
key_must_have_requirements: Expertise in NHP immunology/virology or spatial-omics analysis
Ability to develop and interpret complex human-relevant models
jobs.why_good_match: The radiation-toxicity plus Organ Chip combination is unusually specific to the user's existing radiation-on-chip work, while spatial omics would add a valuable new capability.
gaps_or_risks: NHP immunology and virology are not current core strengths
The role may prioritize spatial-omics expertise more heavily than general scRNA-seq experience
resume_tailoring: Lead with radiation-on-chip rather than Crohn's disease
Show the experimental + computational integration clearly
Frame spatial-omics as the deliberate capability to add
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply immediately because the encouraged application date is September 9.

jobs.title: FDA Postdoctoral Fellowship in Comparative Toxicological Evaluation Using Human Lung Organoid Models
jobs.company: FDA National Center for Toxicological Research / ORISE
jobs.company_info: FDA NCTR conducts regulatory science and toxicology research supporting human-health decision making.
jobs.term: Full-time postdoctoral research appointment; rolling review

salary.note: ORISE stipend based on education and experience; exact amount not surfaced.

jobs.posting_status: Rolling review; application deadline November 20, 2026 at 3 PM ET
jobs.job_description: Develop and apply human lung organoid models for comparative toxicological evaluation of tobacco smoke and electronic nicotine delivery-system aerosols.
key_must_have_requirements: Doctoral training in a relevant biomedical discipline
Strong cell/organoid culture and toxicology research capability
Rigorous experimental design and quantitative data analysis
preferred_requirements: Organoid or advanced human model systems
jobs.why_good_match: This would add regulatory-science credibility while directly leveraging the user's exposure-injury modeling, oxidative-stress assays and human-relevant NAM experience.
gaps_or_risks: Lung biology and tobacco toxicology are new areas
A fellowship may offer less compensation than industry
resume_tailoring: Emphasize exposure-response modeling and regulatory relevance
Translate radiation work into general toxicology methodology
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply early rather than waiting for the November deadline because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Scholar Research — Cardiovascular 3D Printing & Bio-Innovation Laboratory
jobs.company: University of South Florida Health Heart Institute
jobs.company_info: The Ruberg Cardiovascular 3D Printing & Bio-Innovation Laboratory integrates stem-cell biology, 3D printing, bioprinting and tissue engineering.

salary.note: Current posting did not surface a reliable salary.

jobs.job_description: Lead cell-based research and experimental development in a new laboratory combining 3D bioprinting, tissue engineering and regenerative cardiovascular research.
key_must_have_requirements: Independent data analysis and scientific communication
jobs.why_good_match: This is one of the best opportunities to turn the user's existing 3D-printing and microfabrication experience into a true biomedical specialization rather than a supporting skill.
gaps_or_risks: Direct bioprinting and bioink formulation may be limited
Cardiovascular biology is outside the current GI focus
A new lab can offer ownership but may have less established infrastructure
resume_tailoring: Use a fabrication-forward CV and one-page visual portfolio
Explain the transfer from microfluidics to biofabrication
Ask whether the postdoc can own a platform rather than merely operate equipment
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply this month and use the first interview to test project ownership and publication independence.

jobs.title: Research Senior Associate — Comprehensive Cancer Center
jobs.company: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center
jobs.company_info: The Surgical Oncology research program is hiring a specialist/technical expert in molecular biology and organoid research.

salary.note: Salary not disclosed in the employer listing.

jobs.job_description: Develop and manage organoid research projects, conduct complex cell and organoid experiments, perform molecular assays and implement new research methods within surgical oncology.
key_must_have_requirements: qPCR, immunofluorescence, immunoblot, ELISA and related methods
jobs.why_good_match: This is a strong Ohio-based organoid role with a short technical ramp and good overlap with patient-derived models and molecular characterization.
gaps_or_risks: Oncology is not the primary disease focus
The title may offer less scientific independence than a carefully chosen postdoc
resume_tailoring: Emphasize organoid platform ownership and troubleshooting
Show ability to develop new methods
Clarify publication and project-ownership expectations in the cover letter
jobs.immediate_action_now: Apply if staying in Ohio is strategically valuable, but compare independence carefully against Cincinnati Children's and the Wyss postdoc.

jobs.title: Post Doctoral Scholar — Anesthesiology
jobs.company: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center
jobs.company_info: The Bai laboratory studies environmental and genetic drivers of injury using human stem-cell-derived neural models, cerebral organoids, mitochondrial biology and multi-omics.

salary.note: Salary not disclosed in the current employer listing.

jobs.job_description: Investigate environmental injury and neurodegeneration using human stem-cell-derived neural models, cerebral organoids, mitochondrial/redox biology, multi-omics and bioinformatics.
jobs.why_good_match: Although the organ system changes, the mechanistic overlap with oxidative stress, injury biology, organoids and omics is strong and would add iPSC/neural-model breadth.
gaps_or_risks: Neuroscience is a major disease-area pivot
The move may dilute the user's distinct gut/MPS identity unless the new capability is intentional
resume_tailoring: Frame the move around injury biology and human organoid models
Make the purpose of the organ-system pivot explicit
jobs.immediate_action_now: Investigate the project first; apply only if the lab offers meaningful ownership and training in iPSC/organoid methods that strengthen the future PI niche.

briefings.overall_takeaway: Ohio has two serious academic options this week: Cincinnati Children's is the cleanest direct match, while Ohio State offers organoid and human-model roles with different tradeoffs in independence. Nationally, Wyss is the standout because Organ Chips and radiation toxicity intersect almost exactly with the user's existing expertise.
